rows.evidence: The LibriVox page is titled 'Ten Homilies on the First Epistle of John' (Schaff translation, read by ancientchristian). It lists Homily 1 (1 John 1:1-2:11) through Homily 10 (1 John 5:1-3), with per-homily MP3s and a zip download.

No legitimate free recording found. Augustine's LibriVox author catalogue (37 entries) has no Sermons on Selected Lessons of the NT, and Internet Archive audio, SermonAudio, SermonIndex (text only) and Catholic Culture Audiobooks have no reading of Sermon 90.

No legitimate free recording of Sermon 56 found. LibriVox's Augustine catalogue, Internet Archive audio, SermonAudio feeds and the Catholic Culture Audiobooks feed (213 episodes) list no Lord's Prayer sermon to the competentes.

The Catholic Culture Audiobooks episode 'St. Augustine - Lenten Sermons' says it reads Sermons 205 and 211, the second on forgiveness and reconciliation in Lent. James T. Majewski reads it, the translation is 'courtesy of Catholic University of America Press', and the page has an embedded player and MP3.

No legitimate free recording of Sermon 81 found. Web searches for readings of the sack-of-Rome sermons returned only texts and scholarship, and LibriVox, Internet Archive, SermonAudio and Catholic Culture Audiobooks have no audio of it.

No recording found. Searches return only the Latin text and the 1955 O'Reilly critical edition, with no LibriVox, Internet Archive or ministry audio of De excidio urbis Romae.
